title: GSTP alleviates acute lung injury by S-glutathionylation of KEAP1 and subsequent activation of NRF2 pathway.
authors: Sun, Xiaolin; Guo, Chaorui; Huang, Chunyan; Lv, Ning; Chen, Huili; Huang, Haoyan; Zhao, Yulin; Sun, Shanliang; Zhao, Di; Tian, Jingwei; Chen, Xijing; Zhang, Yongjie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究GSTP通过KEAP1 S-谷胱甘肽化修饰激活NRF2通路缓解急性肺损伤，涉及KEAP1-NRF2蛋白互作及分子对接，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合，方法上仅用分子对接，与课题聚焦的TF-DNA互作建模关联有限。
abstract: Oxidative stress plays an important role in the pathogenesis of acute lung injury (ALI). As a typical post-translational modification triggered by oxidative stress, protein S-glutathionylation (PSSG) is regulated by redox signaling pathways and plays diverse roles in oxidative stress conditions. In this study, we found that GSTP downregulation exacerbated LPS-induced injury in human lung epithelial cells and in mice ALI models, confirming the protective effect of GSTP against ALI both in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, a positive correlation was observed between total PSSG level and GSTP expression level in cells and mice lung tissues. Further results demonstrated that GSTP inhibited KEAP1-NRF2 interaction by promoting PSSG process of KEAP1. By the integration of protein mass spectrometry, molecular docking, and site-mutation validation assays, we identified C434 in KEAP1 as the key PSSG site catalyzed by GSTP, which promoted the dissociation of KEAP1-NRF2 complex and activated the subsequent anti-oxidant genes. In vivo experiments with AAV-GSTP mice confirmed that GSTP inhibited LPS-induced lung inflammation by promoting PSSG of KEAP1 and activating the NRF2 downstream antioxidant pathways. Collectively, this study revealed the novel regulatory mechanism of GSTP in the anti-inflammatory function of lungs by modulating PSSG of KEAP1 and the subsequent KEAP1/NRF2 pathway. Targeting at manipulation of GSTP level or activity might be a promising therapeutic strategy for oxidative stress-induced ALI progression.
abstract_zh: 氧化应激在急性肺损伤（ALI）的发病机制中发挥重要作用。作为氧化应激触发的典型翻译后修饰，蛋白质S-谷胱甘肽化（PSSG）受氧化还原信号通路调控，并在氧化应激条件下发挥多种作用。在本研究中，我们发现GSTP下调加剧了脂多糖（LPS）诱导的人肺上皮细胞损伤及小鼠ALI模型中的损伤，从而在体外和体内均证实了GSTP对ALI的保护作用。此外，在细胞和小鼠肺组织中观察到总PSSG水平与GSTP表达水平之间存在正相关。进一步结果表明，GSTP通过促进KEAP1的PSSG过程抑制KEAP1-NRF2相互作用。通过整合蛋白质质谱、分子对接和位点突变验证实验，我们鉴定出KEAP1中的C434为GSTP催化的关键PSSG位点，该位点促进KEAP1-NRF2复合物解离并激活后续抗氧化基因。使用AAV-GSTP小鼠的体内实验证实，GSTP通过促进KEAP1的PSSG并激活NRF2下游抗氧化通路，抑制LPS诱导的肺部炎症。综上，本研究揭示了GSTP通过调节KEAP1的PSSG及随后的KEAP1/NRF2通路在肺部抗炎功能中的新型调控机制。靶向调控GSTP水平或活性可能成为氧化应激诱导的ALI进展的一种有前景的治疗策略。
